newsitem.title: USA: G7 forex cooperation long-standing policy - Summers.
newsitem.headline: G7 forex cooperation long-standing policy - Summers.

text.p: The Group of Seven's call on Saturday for continued cooperation in currency markets was a statement of general policy and was not intended to refer to current market conditions, a senior U.S. official said.

"That was a general commentary on the policy we've been pursuing for years now," Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told Reuters Financial Television. "The leaders didn't intend any comment with respect to the specific situation of exchange markets right now."

In an economic statement issued on Saturday, the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States asked their finance ministers to continue to cooperate closely in the foreign currency markets.

The G7 leaders also set out specific economic goals for each member country. In particular, they stressed the importance of the United States and the United Kingdom remaining vigilant against inflation.

Summers said that the G7 was not concerned about a resurgence of inflation in the two countries and instead described the leaders' comments as "natural" given the length and strength of the economic expansion in both nations.
"I feel good about the (U.S.) economy," the Treasury official added. "We're going to have a sustainable expansion for a long time to come."
